counselFlags: Sealing is not expungement: North Dakota usually offers sealing or closing, not broad expungement. Sealing limits disclosure of court and prosecution records; it may not delete records or remove records held by BCI, law enforcement, federal systems, private background-check companies, or licensing agencies.

Agency scope: Chapter 12-60.1 sealing does not reach BCI criminal history record information or Criminal Justice Data Information Sharing System data; federal, tribal, out-of-state, and private background-check records are not cleared by North Dakota sealing.

Route scope: The North Dakota petition form says the order closes only records controlled by the North Dakota court system; it does not close records controlled by the prosecutor or law-enforcement entities.

Exclusions: Nonconviction closing under § 12-60.1-05 does not apply if the dismissal was part of a plea agreement involving conviction on another offense, the dismissal was due to a finding the person was not fit to proceed, the not-guilty verdict was due to lack of criminal responsibility, or the case was appealed.

Date split: Nonconviction court record closing under N.D.C.C. § 12-60.1-05: a nonconviction means all charges in the case were dismissed or the person was acquitted of all charges. Orders entered on or after August 1, 2025 close automatically 61 days after the order; earlier orders use a Petition to Close Nonconviction Records.
North Dakota petition verification: confirm the required verification/notarization form and any applicable statute with counsel; the source does not specify one.
Confirm the exact N.D.C.C. § 12-60.1-05 subsection for the petition branch before release.
Filing destination is a governed matter fact; a matter without a judicial district and clerk destination fails closed rather than filing into a defaulted district.
Confirm with the clerk whether the assigned judge sets a hearing or an objection period on a Petition to Close Nonconviction Records.

Attorney review: Excluded offenses, felonies involving violence or intimidation, firearm-disability issues, registration offenses, human-trafficking vacatur, immigration consequences, BCI record issues, unpaid restitution, pending charges, unclear deferred-imposition status, and plea-tied dismissals should trigger attorney review before filing.

filing.accessAfterClosingRule: Access to closed nonconviction court records is limited to the clerk, judge, juvenile commission, criminal justice agency, defendant, defendant's lawyer, state's attorney, or a person with a written judge's order.
filing.copiesRule: File the petition and the proposed order with the clerk of court, and keep a copy of everything filed. If the judge requires service on the prosecuting attorney, serve a copy of the petition and the proposed order and file the proof of service.
filing.destinationBasis: The petition is filed with the clerk of court where the criminal case is filed. The exact clerk office is a governed matter fact (clerkOfCourtDestination); this specification supplies no default and no address.
filing.destinationRule: Nonconviction records use § 12-60.1-05: orders entered on or after August 1, 2025 close automatically after 61 days, while earlier orders use a Petition to Close Nonconviction Records filed with the clerk of court, with no filing fee, where the judge may require service on the prosecutor.
filing.feeRule: Nonconviction closing under § 12-60.1-05 (Petition to Close Nonconviction Records, for pre-August 1, 2025 orders) has no filing fee.
filing.feeWaiverRule: No filing fee may be charged on a Petition to Close Nonconviction Records, so no fee waiver application is part of this packet.
filing.hearingOrObjectionRule: The source for this route states no hearing requirement and no objection period for a Petition to Close Nonconviction Records; it states only that the court must enter the closing order within 10 days if the requirements are met. No hearing date, objection window, or appearance instruction is asserted.
filing.postFilingRule: Nonconviction closing under § 12-60.1-05: for orders entered before August 1, 2025, on a Petition to Close Nonconviction Records the court must enter the closing order within 10 days if eligible, and no filing fee may be charged.
filing.reliefScopeRule: The North Dakota petition form says the order closes only records controlled by the North Dakota court system; it does not close records controlled by the prosecutor or law-enforcement entities.
